stem: Which behavior best reflects cultural humility in nursing practice?

options.A: Apply a previously learned cultural profile to predict the client's preferences without asking about individual differences.
options.B: Avoid reflecting on culture, assumptions, or bias so the nurse's own values cannot influence the interaction.
options.C: Treat completion of cultural-competence training as permanent mastery of the beliefs and preferences of people from that group.
options.D: Use ongoing self-reflection about beliefs, assumptions, bias and power while learning directly from the individual client's experiences, values, beliefs, and preferences.

rationale: HHS Think Cultural Health's CLAS in Nursing program describes cultural humility through continuing self-awareness and patient-centered learning. Nurses are asked to examine their own beliefs and values and become aware of privilege, power, bias, stereotypes, and assumptions, while also getting to know the individual patient's cultural identity and providing care responsive to that person's experiences, values, beliefs, and preferences. Therefore D is correct. A substitutes stereotyping for individual assessment, B rejects the self-reflection required for humility, and C treats cultural learning as fixed mastery rather than an ongoing process.
educational_objective: Practice cultural humility through ongoing self-reflection about assumptions, bias and power and by learning from each individual client's cultural identity, experiences, values, beliefs and preferences rather than relying on stereotypes or presumed mastery.
source_organization: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Minority Health — Think Cultural Health
source_document_title: Culturally and Linguistically Appropriate Services (CLAS) in Nursing; What is CLAS?
source_version_date: CLAS in Nursing released February 13, 2024; current nursing course and HHS CLAS guidance live-rechecked August 16, 2026
source_locator: CLAS in Nursing program overview: cultural competency and cultural humility; Course 2 Self-awareness covers beliefs, values, privilege, power, bias and stereotypes; Course 3 learns the patient's cultural identity; Course 4 responds to patient experiences, values, beliefs and preferences. What is CLAS?: respect the whole individual and respond to individual health needs/preferences.
source_claim_supported: Cultural humility in nursing involves ongoing self-awareness of assumptions/bias/power and individualized learning from and responsiveness to the patient's own experiences, values, beliefs and preferences rather than stereotyping or claiming permanent mastery.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity: assess cultural/spiritual influences, use therapeutic and respectful communication, recognize personal bias/assumptions, and provide individualized psychosocially responsive care.
blueprint_topic: Psychosocial Integrity — cultural humility, bias awareness and individualized care

source_original.stem: Which behavior best reflects cultural humility in nursing practice?

options.A: Apply a previously learned cultural profile to predict the patient’s preferences without asking about individual differences.
options.B: Avoid discussing culture or bias so the nurse’s own values cannot influence the interaction.
options.C: Treat completion of cultural-competence training as permanent mastery of the beliefs of patients from that group.
options.D: Use ongoing self-reflection about bias, power, and assumptions while learning from the individual patient’s experiences, values, and preferences.

source_original.rationale: HHS's CLAS in Nursing program explicitly includes cultural humility and emphasizes self-awareness of beliefs and values as well as privilege, power, bias, and stereotypes, together with learning the patient's cultural identity and responding to the patient's experiences, values, beliefs, and preferences.
source_original.source_detail: Cultural humility includes self-awareness, attention to power and bias, and patient-centered learning Source has no separate formal version identifier in the cited page metadata; live currentness and applicability rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Psychosocial Integrity: mental-health symptom recognition, therapeutic communication, coping, cultural/spiritual influences and psychosocial support as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the cultural-humility construct and key D, strengthened the ongoing self-reflection/individual-learning wording, explicitly included beliefs and assumptions alongside bias/power, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium because the final item tests a defined patient-centered cultural-humility behavior.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current HHS Office of Minority Health Think Cultural Health nursing/CLAS guidance; NCSBN 2026 blueprint
audit_findings.currentness: HHS CLAS nursing course and current nursing education page live-rechecked 2026-08-16
audit_findings.exact_locator: CLAS in Nursing Courses 2-4 and What is CLAS? individual-responsiveness principle
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item uses HHS-supported self-awareness and individualized responsiveness without treating cultural-group information as determinative of an individual's preferences or implying one-time training creates cultural mastery.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because group-based assumptions cannot replace asking and learning about the individual client.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because self-reflection about beliefs, bias and assumptions is a core part of cultural humility.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because cultural humility is not permanent mastery of another group's beliefs/preferences.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only D combines ongoing self-reflection with individualized patient learning/responsiveness.
audit_findings.cueing: All options describe approaches to cultural practice rather than unrelated communication techniques.
audit_findings.blueprint: Psychosocial Integrity — cultural influences, respectful individualized care and bias awareness.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked current HHS Think Cultural Health nursing content, CLAS principles, all alternatives, rationale, objective, ambiguity, cueing and NCSBN Psychosocial Integrity alignment. D remained uniquely correct.
